locations.label: Undo (⌘Z) · hold for edit history · shift-click to reset
Edit & export history for this photo
Toggle grain, halation, bloom & borders all at once
Save back to the file Lightroom handed off — Lightroom will re-import and sync it
Settings — transform, edit settings, view, appearance
Pick photos from your Google Photos library — selection happens in Google's own picker (one-time free setup: see Guide)
Library is stored in this browser only (Safari may purge it after ~7 days unused)
Replicate any Lightroom preset: download this chart, apply the preset to it in Lightroom, export (sRGB, full size), drop the export on the LUT zone above
By default Basic Adjustments apply to every loaded photo. Click to make THIS photo's adjustments independent (e.g. nudge just its exposure), or click again to sync it back to the shared value.
Click a neutral (grey/white) area to auto-correct white balance
One-click levels and white balance from the image histogram

Off: untouched decode. Fast (default): the native Rust-side shadow + chroma-wavelet denoise on linear RAW data, before any tone curve — a few seconds, applies automatically. High: additionally runs a neural (RawNIND UtNet2) denoiser, 25–90s at 24MP — never automatic; press "Denoise now" below, or it runs once at export if selected. Requires reopening this photo (or Denoise now) to take effect. Desktop/RAW only.

Real-photo review (5 ISO 12800 shots vs DxO PureRAW) found full strength can soften fine hair/fur strands more than DxO does, even though flat-area noise removal is comparable or better — lower this if High is smoothing detail you want to keep. Changing it re-arms Denoise now / re-applies at next export.

Uses AHD interpolation, which cleans up dense green/magenta false-color speckle on sunlit water/specular highlights much further than Standard — but it trades away some general chroma-noise headroom elsewhere in the frame, so it's opt-in per photo rather than a global default. Requires reopening this photo to take effect. Desktop only.

Bright specular highlights (sunlit water, glints) sometimes show green/magenta demosaic false-color that no amount of Luminance/Color NR fully removes. Since real highlight color is usually near-neutral anyway, this fades Cb/Cr toward zero from mid-tones (~45%) up through highlights — reaches far enough to cover where the fringing actually sits, so it WILL flatten real color in bright areas too at high amounts. Per-photo only, so it never touches other images.
Click a colour in the photo to target it precisely, then dial in how far the selection spreads with Range.
Shows the EFFECTIVE selection in red — shape combined with the luminance and colour-range gates. The Overlay/Isolate modes draw the shape only.

Desktop only: looks up this exact camera+lens+focal-length in a bundled lens-profile database (lensfun) and geometrically corrects distortion automatically on next RAW load. Falls back to the manual sliders below when no profile match exists.
Copies this photo's crop/rotate/flip/straighten onto every other loaded photo, overwriting theirs
Finds the dominant horizontal or vertical line and levels it. Says so plainly when there isn't one.
Clear region — Auto level goes back to searching the whole frame
Keeps dark areas (eyes, nostrils, deep shadows) from flooding red. 0 = full film behavior.
Neutral white halation instead of the warm film glow — best for black-and-white photos (auto-enabled when a B&W photo is loaded).
Film with no anti-halation backing (remjet) — much stronger, bloomier halos with a yellow→orange→red edge, calibrated to Dehancer's no-remjet look.
Extreme halation — the no-remjet glow pushed ≈5–6× stronger for a heavy, stylised bloom. Implies No remjet.
The sprocket styles are drawn to the real 35mm standard, so they stay correct at any aspect ratio. Load frame… takes any scanned rebate PNG you have a licence to use.
Heal blends the copied area into the surrounding colour. Clone copies it exactly.
Batch tokens: {name} source name, {seq} number in batch, {date} YYYY-MM-DD. Add {nover} to drop the version suffix.
Save the current Quality/Format/Resize/Sharpening as a named preset
Batch only. Solves each photo's own exposure and white balance so the set matches the one you're previewing. Your look is untouched.
Save all slider settings to localStorage
Save the current recipe (everything except crop/geometry) as a named, reusable Style
Import a Style .json exported from Chromasmith
Sign in to Google Photos (lasts ~1 hour)
Set or change your Google OAuth client ID
True 1:1 view — renders a native-resolution crop through the full pipeline so grain & halation appear at real export scale
Full resolution — renders the whole preview at full source resolution instead of the usual capped size. Costs more GPU time; drops to the capped size automatically while dragging a slider
Editor background colour (also right-click the empty area around the photo)
Press and hold to see the original
Choose what the split's before-side compares against
Loop playback within the trim range
Exports the CURRENT frame through the full-res still export path, graded exactly like the video preview. Only as large as the video itself.
Rule-of-thirds + safe-area guides over the preview

Randomly redistribute photos into the slots
Find '+_esc(s.name)+' in this photo and select it. Always check the result — this suggests, it does not guarantee.
More than one '+_esc(s.name)+' in this photo? Look for several distinct locations, each installed as its own mask.
Add the CURRENT selection as another reference photo. More references help, and a varied one helps most.
Check every other loaded photo for '+_esc(s.name)+' (coarse pass — jump to a result and Find again for a real check).

Name this selection so you can find the same subject in other photos. Measured reliability (~77-80% recall on one dog across varied conditions) is a general guide, not a per-species guarantee — a person, a different animal, or a busier scene may do better or worse.
Save every taught subject (names, references, prototypes) as a JSON file — to back up or move to another machine.
Load a subjects file exported from this app (this or another machine). Adds/replaces by name — never deletes an existing subject not in the file.
Jump to this photo and check it yourself — a scan score is not a confidence.
Add this one as an eraser instead — subtracted from every other mask, for building \'every instance except this one\'.
Copies this photo\'s mask set onto every other loaded photo, overwriting theirs
